name: Nethanel
overview: Nethanel was a male official serving under King Jehoshaphat. His role was significant in the religious instruction of the people, as he was sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the law. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Nethanel means 'G-d [El] has given,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that acknowledges God's providence. This proper name, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 17:7, highlights the divine blessing implied in his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Nethanel beyond his official role under Jehoshaphat. There are no noted relatives or tribal connections mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Nethanel's importance lies in his service as an official entrusted with teaching the law during Jehoshaphat's reign, a time of religious reform and renewal. His appointment demonstrates the king's commitment to instructing the people in God's commandments, contributing to the spiritual strengthening of Judah. This role underscores the value placed on biblical teaching and leadership in the community.
